text:
In a quiet town lived a famous tea master. People travelled from far away to learn from him, and many of them hoped to become rich teachers one day.

A young woman named Mei arrived at his house early one morning. “I want to learn everything about tea,” she said. “How long will it take?”

“Ten years,” said the master.

“Ten years? That’s too long! What if I work twice as hard?”

“Then it will take twenty years,” he said calmly.

Mei was surprised and a little angry, but she stayed. For the first year, the master gave her only one job: she washed the cups. She washed them again and again, and she felt bored and frustrated.

One day, she finally asked, “When will I learn the real secrets?”

The master smiled. “Bring me a cup of tea.”

Mei made the tea quickly and gave it to him. He tasted it and shook his head. “You were thinking about tomorrow. I can taste it.”

Mei understood. She made another cup, slowly, thinking only about the water, the leaves and her hands.

The master tasted it again and closed his eyes. “Now,” he said quietly, “you have learned the first secret.”

Moral: Be present in what you are doing right now, because rushing spoils everything.

quiz.q: The master said it would take ten years to learn about tea.
Working twice as hard would make it faster.
What was Mei's only job in the first year?
What was wrong with Mei's first cup of tea?
Be ___ in what you are doing right now.
